q: Standard deviation as a risk measure captures:
o: Total risk (variation in periodic returns vs scheme's own average)
e: Standard deviation measures total risk — fluctuation in periodic returns relative to the scheme's own average return. Higher SD = greater volatility.

q: Beta of the market index, by definition, is:
e: The diversified market index has Beta = 1 by definition. Beta > 1 means the security/scheme is more volatile than the market; Beta < 1 means less volatile.

q: A scheme with Beta of 1.2 will move __ when the market moves by 10%.
e: Beta of 1.2 means the scheme moves 12% (1.2 × 10%) for a 10% market movement, both up and down.

q: Beta as a risk measure is most relevant for:
e: Beta — based on CAPM and systematic risk — is most relevant for equity schemes. Less meaningful for debt or commodity schemes.

q: Modified Duration measures:
o: Sensitivity of debt security value to interest rate changes
e: Modified Duration measures the price sensitivity of a debt security to changes in interest rates. Higher MD = greater interest-rate risk.

q: In annualizing the standard deviation calculated on weekly returns, you multiply by:
e: Weekly SD × sqrt(52) annualizes it. Monthly returns × sqrt(12); Daily returns × sqrt(252) (trading days).

q: Which type of risk CAN be reduced through diversification across unrelated securities?
e: Specific (unsystematic) risk can be reduced via diversification. Systematic / market-wide risk cannot.

q: Side-pocketing (segregated portfolio) in a mutual fund scheme is invoked when:
o: A debt instrument in the portfolio faces a credit event (default/rating downgrade)
Investor base grows beyond a level
e: Segregated portfolio (side-pocketing) is created on a credit event in a debt instrument — to ring-fence the affected security from the main portfolio.

q: According to SEBI, restriction on redemption (gating) may be imposed for a maximum of:
e: Gating may be imposed only for a maximum of 10 working days in any 90-day period, with Board of AMC + Trustees approval, and SEBI must be informed.

q: When redemption restriction (gating) is imposed, redemptions up to ___ must be processed without restriction:
e: Up to ₹2 lakhs must be redeemed without restriction. Amounts above ₹2 lakhs are subject to the gating; the first ₹2 lakh of each request is processed normally.

q: Reinvestment risk in a debt portfolio refers to:
o: Risk that the issuer will default
Risk that interim cash flows are reinvested at lower rates than originally assumed
Risk that the AMC will close the scheme
e: Reinvestment risk is the risk that interim cash flows (coupons, partial redemptions) are reinvested at rates lower than originally assumed.

q: A scheme can hold a maximum of __ of its NAV in securities issued by a single issuer.
e: SEBI regulations cap exposure to a single issuer at 10% of NAV (with limited extensions for select instruments under board approvals).

q: Systematic risk is also referred to as:
e: Systematic risk = market risk = non-diversifiable risk. Affects all securities; cannot be eliminated through diversification.

q: Per finance theory, investors are rewarded for taking:
e: Investors are compensated only for non-diversifiable (systematic) risk. Diversifiable risk can be eliminated for free via diversification, so the market doesn't reward taking it.

q: A scheme is described as a "pass-through vehicle" because:
o: All investment risks are passed onto unitholders, who are the beneficial owners
e: In a mutual fund, all gains and risks pass through to unitholders, who are the beneficial owners of the trust. Unlike an FD, the AMC does not promise a fixed return.

q: A side-pocket (segregated portfolio) gets created when:
o: A debt instrument in the portfolio faces a credit event (downgrade/default)
Investor base grows above a threshold
e: On a credit event in a debt instrument (rating downgrade below investment grade or default), the AMC can create a segregated portfolio to ring-fence the affected security.

q: In a segregated portfolio, the affected security is:
o: Carved out into a separate portfolio; only existing unitholders at cut-off get units; no fresh inflows allowed
e: On segregation, only unitholders existing at the credit-event date receive units in the segregated portfolio. Recoveries (when realised) are distributed pro-rata.

q: Which is the most accurate description of Variance as a risk measure?
e: Variance = SD². Equivalently, SD = sqrt(Variance). Both measure dispersion of returns from the mean.

q: Weighted Average Maturity in a debt scheme indicates:
o: Interest rate sensitivity at portfolio level
e: WAM at portfolio level indicates interest rate sensitivity. Higher WAM = higher sensitivity to interest rate changes (similar to Modified Duration).

q: Unsystematic risk can be reduced through diversification. True or False?
e: TRUE. Unsystematic (company-specific) risk is diversifiable. Systematic (market-wide) risk cannot be reduced through diversification.

q: Which is a measure of fluctuation in periodic returns of an equity mutual fund scheme?
e: Variance (and its square root, Standard Deviation) measures the fluctuation in periodic returns. Sharpe and Alpha are risk-ADJUSTED return measures. Modified Duration applies to debt.

The relationship between Macaulay Duration (MacD) and Modified Duration (ModD) is:
o: ModD = MacD / (1 + YTM/n) — ModD slightly less than MacD
e: ModD = MacD / (1 + YTM/n) where n is compounding frequency. ModD is always slightly less than MacD. ModD measures price sensitivity directly; MacD measures weighted average time to receive cash flows.

q: Convexity, as a bond risk measure:
o: Measures the curvature of price-yield relationship — refines duration's linear approximation for large rate changes
e: Convexity captures the second-order (curvature) relationship between bond prices and yields. Duration alone is a linear approximation; convexity refines it for large rate moves.

q: A scheme with high credit rating profile (e.g., 80% AAA, 20% AA) has:
e: AAA is the highest credit rating; AA is also investment grade. Higher allocation to AAA = lower credit risk. Doesn't affect interest rate risk directly.

q: A scheme can hold a maximum of ___ of its NAV in securities issued by a SINGLE issuer (debt):
e: SEBI single-issuer cap: 10% in debt securities of a single issuer (extendable to 12% with specific board approvals). Reduces concentration risk.

q: A scheme's exposure to a "Group" (related parties) of issuers is capped at:
e: Group exposure cap: typically 25% of NAV for debt securities issued by entities within the same business group. Prevents concentration in a single group's credit.

q: Side-pocketing (segregated portfolio) — only investors holding units AT THE TIME OF the credit event:
o: Receive units in the segregated portfolio; future buyers do NOT get exposure to the affected security
e: Only existing unitholders at the credit-event cut-off date receive units in the segregated portfolio. New investors entering after that date are not exposed to the legacy bad asset.

q: Recoveries from a side-pocketed (segregated) instrument are:
o: Distributed pro-rata to unitholders of the segregated portfolio
e: Any recovery from the segregated security (when it pays back, partially or fully) is distributed pro-rata to the unitholders of the segregated portfolio.

q: Gating (restriction on redemption) — the first ___ of any redemption request must be processed without restriction:
e: Per SEBI: first ₹2 lakhs of any redemption request is processed without gating. Amounts above ₹2 lakhs are subject to the restriction.

q: Gating can be invoked for a maximum of:
e: Gating: max 10 working days in any 90-day period. Requires Board of AMC + Trustees approval. SEBI must be informed immediately. Used only for systemic crises.

q: For a scheme to qualify as Conservative Hybrid (10-25% equity), the average exposure is computed:
e: Equity exposure for hybrid categorisation is typically measured on a quarterly average basis to avoid daily breach issues from market volatility.

q: Stress testing for liquid funds (SEBI mandate) requires:
o: Periodic simulation of large redemption scenarios + portfolio liquidity assessment
e: SEBI mandates AMCs to conduct stress tests on liquid funds — simulating large redemption pressure and assessing portfolio liquidity. Results disclosed periodically.

q: The Riskometer of a scheme can change based on portfolio composition. AMC must:
o: Re-evaluate monthly + communicate any change to unitholders via notice-cum-addendum + SMS/email
e: Riskometer must be re-evaluated monthly. Any change must be communicated via notice-cum-addendum AND SMS/email to unitholders. Transparency is mandatory.

q: A scheme triggers gating when redemption requests exceed liquidity. The first ₹2 lakhs of every request:
e: SEBI rule: first ₹2 lakhs of any redemption request must be processed without restriction during gating. Only excess above ₹2 lakhs is subject to gating.

q: Modified Duration is approximately related to Macaulay Duration as:
e: ModD = MacD ÷ (1 + YTM/n). ModD is slightly less than MacD and gives direct price-sensitivity to rate changes.

q: A scheme can hold up to ___ of its NAV in securities of a single issuer (debt):
e: SEBI single-issuer cap: 10% of NAV in debt of a single issuer, extendable to 12% with specific approvals.

q: Beta of the market index, by definition:
e: Market index Beta = 1 by definition. Schemes/securities are measured relative to the market.

q: When a debt instrument in a scheme's portfolio faces a credit event (downgrade/default), AMC may invoke:
o: Side-pocketing (segregated portfolio) — affected security carved out
e: On a credit event, AMC may create a segregated portfolio for the affected security. Existing unitholders get units in both main and segregated portfolios.
